subject.title: Feature Request: Memory Trust Tagging by Source

question: Should OpenClaw make framework-assigned memory provenance and influence policy a native contract for its recommended memory path, and which component should own trust assignment and enforcement?
rationale: This changes a persistent security boundary and public memory/plugin contracts; external integrations prove feasibility, but automation cannot choose the durable owner, secure defaults, migration model, or authority for trust promotion.

options.title: Native provenance contract
options.body: Adopt framework-assigned source provenance first, then add explicit review, retention, and influence policy to the recommended memory plugin with migrations.

options.title: External governed memory
options.body: Keep builtin memory source-only and document maintained plugin or MCP implementations for deployments requiring governed memory.

options.title: Attribution only
options.body: Limit native work to actor and source provenance while deferring trust scoring, expiry, and influence enforcement.

recommendation.title: Native provenance contract
recommendation.body: Adopt framework-assigned source provenance first, then add explicit review, retention, and influence policy to the recommended memory plugin with migrations.

likelyOwner.reason: The prior issue review and memory host contract history make this the strongest available owner for the cross-backend security decision.
